transcript:
Meeting: Novara Health - Procurement MSA & DPA Review
Date: 2025-09-18
Start: 14:30 PDT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Das (Redwood SE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood Solutions), James Li (Novara - Head of Procurement), Sofia Romero (Novara - Legal Counsel), Anika Patel (Novara - Security Lead), Darren Cole (Novara - Eng Mgr)

Summary: Quick run through of MSA redlines, DPA specifics (data residency, KMS), SLA targets, and procurement/PO process. Agreed Redwood to send redlined MSA and SOC2 link; security follow-up requested.

Topics: MSA liability/indemnity; data processing terms; SLA credits; onboarding and invoicing; pilot/pricing; security artifacts (SOC2, pen test, KMS)

Action items (captured in metadata above)

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:05] Alex Morgan: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. um so today the plan is, Sofia, James, we want to walk through the MSA redlines you sent and the DPA points, make sure we're aligned on SLAs and procurement steps. Does that sound right?
[00:00:18] James Li: Yeah that's right. We've got a few key must-haves from procurement, but legal also has some comments on indemnity and data residency.
[00:00:25] Sofia Romero: Correct. We mainly want to confirm the liability cap, data processing terms, and something about audit rights. I'll jump in with specifics when we hit those sections.
[00:00:33] Priya Das: Great. I'll be covering the technical aspects, like how Redwood Dedicated vs Redwood Private behaves, and the options for KMS/HSM and data segregation.
[00:00:40] Marco Alvarez: I'll handle onboarding and billing questions if they come up.
[00:00:44] Darren Cole: And I'll be here for engineering questions. We may also want a deeper technical deep dive later.

[00:01:10] Alex Morgan: Ok first on the MSA liability cap — you redlined a cap at two times annual fees and asked for carveouts for gross negligence. Our standard is one times annual fees, with statutory exceptions. Sofia, could you restate your team's ask?
[00:01:25] Sofia Romero: Yes — procurement prefers two times ARR, legal prefers higher for certain data breach scenarios. We also asked for mutual indemnity on third-party claims, and a carveout for willful misconduct.
[00:01:40] Alex Morgan: Understood. We can escalate that with our legal, but historically the cap negotiations are back-and-forth and can take a few cycles. We'll send a redline that shows alternatives (1x with certain carveouts vs 2x).
[00:01:52] James Li: Practically speaking for procurement we need to know the range so we can get approvals. If Redwood can show a 1x plus carveouts is typical, that's OK, but we need the paperwork soon.

[00:02:18] Priya Das: On the DPA side, Anika asked about data residency and encryption. Redwood supports hosted deployments in multi regions, and for Novara's PHI workloads we recommend Redwood Private in your VPC or on-prem option. That gives you customer-managed network and optional KMS integration.
[00:02:35] Anika Patel: Can you confirm key management — we need a BYOK flow, HSM-backed keys, and we need to ensure key material never leaves our control.
[00:02:43] Priya Das: Yes, we have a BYOK flow. For Redwood Private we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS, HSMs). We'll include the KMS integration doc; note that some early notes might say KV cache or 'KV cash' in the transcript, that was a wacky STT. The KV cache is in-memory on the runtime but encrypted at rest for dedicated variants — in Private you control the keys.
[00:03:05] Anika Patel: Good, we also need to know retention and deletion guarantees — like can you guarantee deletion of cached prompts and logs within X days?
[00:03:13] Priya Das: We can commit to configurable retention. For Private you can set TTLs or full deletion on request; for Dedicated we have options to purge logs within 30 days or shorter with an add-on. We'll provide the deletion SLAs in the DPA appendix.

[00:03:45] Sofia Romero: On audit rights — we asked for SOC2 Type II and pen test reports. Is the SOC2 report up to date?
[00:03:52] Marco Alvarez: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II for the inference platform, last audited 2025-06. We'll share the report link and a redacted pen test summary. There may be NDAs needed for full penetration test details.
[00:04:06] Anika Patel: NDAs are fine. Also, we need to understand encryption in transit and at rest, and whether any PII is stored on long-term storage.
[00:04:14] Priya Das: Encryption in transit is TLS 1.2/1.3, at rest is AES-256; model KV caches are ephemeral but when backed to disk in some flows they are encrypted. We'll include a technical appendix that clarifies ephemeral vs persisted storage.

[00:04:35] James Li: About SLAs — we saw your standard 99.9% uptime with credits. For our B2B customers we need a 99.95 target for critical endpoints. Is there a higher SLA or dedicated offering?
[00:04:45] Alex Morgan: Yes, Redwood Dedicated can be deployed with stronger SLOs and we offer SLA-backed commitments on Dedicated/Private contracts. The 99.95 is achievable on Dedicated with reserved GPU pools and mutual testing. Pricing differs, of course.
[00:04:58] James Li: Ok procurement will want the cost delta documented.
[00:05:10] Darren Cole: On the engineering side, about fallbacks — does Redwood have model fallback or routing if a zone is down? We can't have silent failure during peak times.
[00:05:18] Priya Das: We do smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants or alternate regions. For Private that's within your cluster; for Hosted we route across regions and can failover to Dedicated if configured. There is some complexity around prompt consistency — we'll document tradeoffs.

[00:05:40] Sofia Romero: Back to the MSA, there's a clause around export controls and restricted data. We need explicit language that we won't be required to host certain restricted content on Redwood-hosted infra in locations we've not agreed to.
[00:05:50] Alex Morgan: We can add an export control section that mirrors standard cloud provider language; we'll prepare the redline.

[00:06:12] James Li: Procurement items — PO process, invoice cadence, and tax info. We need a sample invoice and whether Redwood accepts P-card or only wire/ACH.
[00:06:20] Marco Alvarez: We accept ACH and wire, P-card for smaller deals depending on finance. We'll attach a billing guide and sample invoice. Standard net 30 unless negotiated.
[00:06:33] James Li: Great. Also need to confirm whether Redwood requires an initial commit for Dedicated or if pilot can run hosted with a conversion to Dedicated later.
[00:06:40] Alex Morgan: You can pilot on hosted with usage-based pricing, then move to Dedicated with a committed capacity contract. We typically do a 30-90 day pilot, then a committed Dedicated proposal if you want sustained SLA and cost predictability.

[00:07:05] Anika Patel: Regarding data subject requests and deletion, we need to be able to demonstrate deletion for audit. How do you record deletion actions?
[00:07:12] Priya Das: We log deletion requests and produce audit logs. For Private you control logs; for Hosted we provide exportable logs and an API to confirm deletion with request IDs. We'll include an example API call in the appendix.

[00:07:40] Sofia Romero: Indemnity language — we asked for mutual indemnity for IP and third-party claims, and clearer obligations in case of breach. Is Redwood prepared to make changes?
[00:07:49] Alex Morgan: We'll ask legal to propose mutual indemnity with certain limitations. Historically Redwood offers IP indemnity for customer use under normal terms but not for misuse. We'll provide two redline options.

[00:08:12] James Li: Timeline — procurement needs a finalized MSA within two weeks to make quarter-end budget approvals. Can Redwood target that?
[00:08:20] Alex Morgan: We'll aim to have a redlined MSA back by 2025-09-22. If legal talks escalate we may need an extra week but we'll flag you immediately.

[00:08:45] Marco Alvarez: Quick note on onboarding: once MSA & PO are signed we usually do a kickoff, 2-week technical onboarding with SE support, and then a pilot monitoring period. We'll share the onboarding checklist.

[00:09:10] Darren Cole: For the pilot we'd like to test latencies on our worst-case sequences and run some regression evals. Can Redwood run a small benchmark or provide perf profiles?
[00:09:18] Priya Das: Yes — we can run a perf benchmark with a small sample set or share previously measured latency/cost sheets for models similar to what you plan to use. We'll need sample prompts and expected QPS.

[00:09:40] Sofia Romero: On the DPA we had a clause about subcontractors and subprocessors. We need a subprocessor list and process for notification and objection.

[00:09:47] Alex Morgan: We'll include the current subprocessor list and the process for objections. We typically notify when a new subprocessor is added and provide a window for objections, but some customers ask for approval rights — we'll note that in the redline.

[00:10:12] James Li: A couple more procurement details: does Redwood do standard 3rd-party vendor questionnaires (security questionnaires) or do you expect us to fill in custom forms?
[00:10:20] Marco Alvarez: We can provide an attestation and we often fill standard security questionnaires (SIG, or a shorter vendor risk form). For lengthy custom forms we may request an NDA first.

[00:10:40] Alex Morgan: Let's talk pricing approvals — James, what's your procurement timeline? Do you need a committed quote or is a pilot quote fine?

[00:10:47] James Li: For budget we need a committed quote to present to finance. Pilot pricing is fine for initial technical approval but not for contract. So we need both: pilot rates and a committed Dedicated pricing sheet.

[00:11:05] Priya Das: We'll prepare a pilot pricing worksheet and a sample Dedicated commitment proposal. Expect that in the packet with the redlined MSA.

[00:11:30] Sofia Romero: Also, confidentiality — can we get a mutual NDA attached to the MSA for sharing sensitive artifacts like the full pen test?

[00:11:38] Alex Morgan: Yes, we can include mutual NDA language or attach a separate NDA. We'll include an NDA where needed before sharing sensitive docs.

[00:12:00] Anika Patel: One operational question — how do you handle incident notifications for security incidents and required SLA reporting cadence?

[00:12:08] Priya Das: We have an incident response runbook; for customers on Dedicated/Private we provide direct pager/email alerts and a security contact. For Hosted we have a standard incident notification timeline and public status page with updates. We'll include the incident response SLA in the DPA appendix.

[00:12:40] Sofia Romero: We have a redline on termination for convenience — procurement wants a 60-day termination for convenience on pilot, legal prefers 90. Thoughts?

[00:12:48] Alex Morgan: For pilots we can often agree to 30-60 days; for committed Dedicated contracts 90 days is typical. We'll show both options in the redlined MSA.

[00:13:12] James Li: If we get legal signoff on the MSA redline, what's the approval path for finance? Do you provide SOWs for pilots and then invoice?

[00:13:20] Marco Alvarez: Yes — we'll generate an SOW for the pilot with scope, timelines, and estimated cost. Once signed, we issue invoice per the SOW terms.

[00:13:45] Darren Cole: On telemetry — what logging will be available to us during the pilot? Request IDs, latency per request, and token usage?

[00:13:53] Priya Das: We provide request-level logs (with obfuscation options), request IDs, latency, and token usage. For privacy reasons we can mask user content by default or provide an opt-in for raw text logs.

[00:14:20] Sofia Romero: There's an IP clause we flagged about ownership of prompts and outputs. Novara wants explicit language that Novara owns prompts and outputs; Redwood needs to retain model weights and improvements.

[00:14:29] Alex Morgan: That's standard; we can clarify customer data ownership in the MSA/DPA and the model IP remains Redwood's. We'll add language to the DPA.

[00:14:55] James Li: Any special terms for healthcare data / PHI? We need to be sure about HIPAA compliance and BAA.

[00:15:03] Priya Das: Redwood supports HIPAA workflows on Private/Dedicated and we can sign a BAA for PHI workloads. For hosted we have limited support depending on region and configuration — we'll map options in the appendix.

[00:15:30] Anika Patel: For the BAA we need clarity on breach notification timing and roles.

[00:15:35] Alex Morgan: We'll include 72-hour notification and the roles in the BAA draft.

[00:16:00] Marco Alvarez: Quick note on onboarding resources: we'll assign a Customer Success Manager once the SOW is signed, and SE time is provisioned for the 2-week kickoff.

[00:16:25] James Li: For procurement we need to know the exact legal entity to put on the PO. Which Redwood entity signs the MSA?

[00:16:32] Alex Morgan: The master contracting entity is Redwood Inference, Inc., based in Delaware. We'll include full legal and tax details in the docs pack.
[00:16:55] Sofia Romero: A question about subprocessor locations — we need to ensure no data is routed to countries on our restricted list. Can you provide a current list of data center regions?

[00:17:03] Priya Das: Yes; for Hosted we will list available regions and default routing. For Private you control the VPC region. We'll provide a map and the current subprocessor geographic footprint.

[00:17:30] James Li: Ok let's fast-forward — what's the concrete timeline and deliverables we expect this week?

[00:17:36] Alex Morgan: Deliverables: redlined MSA + DPA draft, SOC2 link, pricing worksheet, onboarding checklist, and KMS integration doc. Target delivery: 2025-09-22.

[00:17:50] James Li: That aligns with procurement. We'll review and circulate to finance/legal.

[00:18:10] Anika Patel: One more security note: do you support customer-managed logging retention periods and are logs encrypted with customer keys?

[00:18:18] Priya Das: For Private yes; for Dedicated we can offer customer-managed key options for logs. We'll detail which logs are encrypted with customer keys vs Redwood-managed keys.

[00:18:45] Sofia Romero: If we see any blockers on indemnity or liability, can we escalate to legal contacts? Who at Redwood would that be?

[00:18:52] Alex Morgan: I'll introduce you to our GC, Mia Chen, and to our contracts lead. We'll CC them on the redline.

[00:19:15] Darren Cole: On performance testing — we may want a short-run benchmark on our traffic shape. How does Redwood ingest sample traffic?

[00:19:22] Priya Das: We take a small sample dataset and a load profile. For hosted we can run a bench using our inference API endpoints; for Private we run within the cluster. Expect a short lead time to schedule if we need heavy GPU time.

[00:19:48] James Li: Anything else from the team?

[00:19:52] Marco Alvarez: No, just to reiterate we'll send billing and sample invoice.

[00:19:56] Sofia Romero: Please include the pen test redacted summary under NDA.

[00:20:02] Alex Morgan: Yep. We'll include that.

[00:20:30] [Speaker 1, unintelligible]: mm-hmm
[00:20:40] [00:20:40] Alex Morgan: Ok I think we covered most of it. Quick recap — Redwood action: redline MSA/DPA, SOC2 link, pen test summary under NDA, pricing sheets, KMS doc, onboarding checklist. Novara action: review, provide custom security questionnaire and list of restricted countries.

[00:21:05] James Li: Correct. We'll aim to get our first round of feedback within 48 hours of receiving the redline.

[00:21:30] Alex Morgan: Great. Do we want to schedule a security follow-up? Anika, what week works for you?

[00:21:35] Anika Patel: Week of 2025-09-29 works. Prefer morning PT.

[00:21:50] Alex Morgan: I'll propose two slots after we send the redline.

[00:22:12] Sofia Romero: One last question — data deletion proof for auditors: can you provide a sample deletion certificate?

[00:22:20] Priya Das: We can provide a deletion confirmation with request ID and timestamp, and include retention reports for that period. We'll attach a sample.

[00:22:45] James Li: Sounds good. Thank you everyone.
[00:22:50] Alex Morgan: Thanks all, look forward to next steps.

[00:54:30] Meeting ended

Notes: Transcript contains some STT artifacts (e.g., 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache', speaker labels sometimes generic). Participants requested redlines, SOC2, pen test summary, and pricing. Next meeting: security follow-up week of 2025-09-29.
